reasons: § 2.1 is a three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay expressly 'without reduction or termination rights' — the rule's walk-away position, so a deviation finding is correctly classified and not an over-flag of an acceptable fallback.

The redline substitutes pay-for-use language, which is exactly the redline guidance ('delete or narrow'); the high changed-character ratio is expected because the entire commitment sentence must be replaced, and no narrower edit could remove a take-or-pay obligation drafted as an unqualified commitment.

The comment accurately states what changed, cites the playbook prohibition on multi-year commitments with no reduction/termination right, and offers the fallback (12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up rather than penalty), matching the required tone and prefix.

The finding is directionally correct for the customer (removes an obligation on our party) and does not duplicate another commercial term; references to §§ 9.4/12.3 are supporting context rather than the basis of the flag.
